transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 28 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (SableCore CTO), Carlos Mendes (SableCore ML Eng), Dana Li (SableCore Infra), Jordan Park (SableCore Product)
Shared links: https://redwood.app/bench/sablecore-2027-11-01, https://drive.redwood/bench-spreadsheet/sablecore-raw.csv

Summary (auto): Redwood p50 42ms vs incumbent 67ms; p95 130ms vs incumbent 210ms. Throughput ~780 tok/s vs incumbent ~445 tok/s on the same harness. Some noise on p95 attributed to KV cache warmup and uneven batching; SE to run extended head-to-head. Next: 2h load test, pricing sketch for dedicated slot, confirm SSO/peering windows.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna do a short readout — Liam will run through the numbers, then we'll cover root cause and next steps. Um, Priya, thanks for carving out time.
[00:17] Priya: Yeah thanks, quick ask, keep it tight, we've got exec time at 4:30 so appreciate the precision.
[00:34] Liam: Cool, I'll jump in. So high level on the bench — we ran the same harness you gave us with the trimmed prompt set, 95th length distribution you sent, and we compared against your incumbent, "IncumbentAI". The results: p50 latency for Redwood was 42ms, incumbent 67ms. p95 was 130ms vs 210ms. Throughput steady-state measured as tokens per second was ~780 tok/s on Redwood vs ~445 tok/s on the incumbent on identical VM counts.
[01:05] Carlos: Wait, 780? That seems high relative to earlier numbers, are we looking at single-GPU numbers or aggregated?
[01:12] Liam: Good call. This is aggregated across the four-card pool we provisioned for the test (same vCPU/GPU ratio as the incumbent run). Per-GPU it's roughly 195 tok/s; the aggregate is the 780. I should have called out aggregation — sorry.
[01:28] Jordan: And the prompt mix is the 60/30/10 short/med/long distribution we shared?
[01:34] Liam: Exactly. Carlos, I also added the warmup phase — first seven minutes had KV cache population, so there was tail noise.
[01:45] Dana: So the p95 delta — is that mostly warmup or do you see steady tail issues too?
[01:51] Liam: Mostly warmup and some batching skew when two big requests collide. We saw a pattern where a long request would flush the batching window and cause a 200-300ms spike, that's what pushed the p95 up. When we enabled small dynamic batching tweaks and adjusted the tolerable window, p95 came down to the 120–140ms band.
[02:10] Priya: Okay, that aligns with what our ops saw. But we'd like to see head-to-head under continuous load for longer. A 30-minute run isn't enough for us to sign off.
[02:18] Maya: Totally — that's why Liam proposed the 2-hour head-to-head with 500 concurrent sessions, to exercise KV cache churn and steady-state.
[02:25] Priya: 500 concurrent— that's close to our worst-case. Fine. Carlos, can you get the production sample prompts ready?
[02:30] Carlos: Yeah I'll extract a 10k sample and share. The only caveat is some prompts have streaming expectations — will we test streaming as well?
[02:37] Liam: We can do streaming, but for this run let's do both modes: a 90% non-stream baseline and a 10% streaming set to reproduce your mix. We'll publish the script so it's reproducible.
[02:46] Dana: Network — we still need VPC peering and SSO confirmation. We have a maintenance window Friday; can Redwood do the peering then?
[02:54] Maya: We can. Our private deployment engineers are available Friday 02:00–06:00 UTC, is that in scope?
[03:02] Dana: That window works. Also security: will you share SOC2 cert and KMS integration docs again? Legal wants to see audit log detail.
[03:10] Maya: Yep, I will send the SOC2 letter and the KMS integration guide. Also, we have an audit logs walkthrough doc — I'll drop links.
[03:18] Priya: One more thing on cost — how would dedicated slot pricing compare to continuing with hosted? If the performance delta is good, we might be ok paying for predictability.
[03:27] Maya: I'll sketch a pricing outline for a Dedicated footprint with a reserved 4-card pool plus burst, and show run-rate vs usage-based hosted. Rough ballpark in the email, final numbers after we see the 2h run.
[03:36] Priya: Cool.
[03:39] Liam: Back to the bench — we noticed quantization choices changed checksum per-token latency a bit. On q4_0 we saw slightly lower latency but a mild quality delta for some edge prompts. We can keep your quant profile at q4_hybrid that you specified, or push q4_0 if you want more latency savings.
[03:56] Carlos: We care more about fidelity on our long-tail legal prompts, so probably keep hybrid. Can you quantify the perf delta?
[04:03] Liam: Yeah — hybrid vs q4_0 traded about 8–12% lower p50 on q4_0 but some drop in BLEU-like ngram recall on a small eval set. We'll attach the eval snippets.
[04:15] Priya: Make sure the eval snippets don't include PII — remove anything sensitive.
[04:20] Maya: Good catch. We'll scrub before sharing.
[04:24] Jordan: Any notes about routing/fallback during maintenance? We can't have 30s outages.
[04:28] Liam: We recommend a short grace window and automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model during maintenance. Redwood's routing policy can do canary + fallback so requests don't error — they'll degrade to a cheaper variant if capacity is constrained. That tradeoff keeps availability but might slightly change token cost/quality.
[04:45] Dana: For compliance, we need audit logs that show per-request model, user, timestamps. Is that captured?
[04:51] Maya: Yes, audit logs include request id, model version, routing decision, tenant id, timestamp; we can show a sample.
[04:58] Priya: Great. So immediate next actions?
[05:02] Maya: Liam runs the 2h head-to-head (Friday slot or earlier) — we aim for Friday. I will send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs tomorrow. Carlos to share prod prompts. Dana to confirm peering window. We reconvene after the 2h run to decide on dedicated commit.
[05:18] Priya: Sounds good, thanks.
[05:21] Jordan: Two quick clarifying things: 1) is the throughput number including tokenization overhead? 2) will the logs include per-token tokenization time?
[05:30] Liam: Throughput includes tokenizer time. We can give breakdown — tokenization vs model vs network. Per-token times will be in the raw logs but not in the condensed summary — we can include a column for tokenizer times in the shared CSV.
[05:42] Carlos: Also, curious about memory pressure — did you see any OOMs or evictions during long runs?
[05:48] Liam: No OOMs on the pool we used. There were cache evictions as expected during churn, but nothing fatal. We should still run the long exercise to confirm at scale.
[05:59] Priya: Okay last thing — competitor angle. If we go dedicated with Redwood, what's the migration path if we need on-prem later?
[06:08] Maya: We support Private deployments including customer-managed VPC and an on-prem package. Migration is mostly model pinning and network cutover; our Solutions team will draft a migration checklist.
[06:19] Priya: Nice. That's it from my side.
[06:22] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[06:27] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and minor gaps; product names sometimes transcribed as "RedWood" or "red wood"; some timestamps approximate.
